boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: A no-admission museum outing with distinct galleries, landmarks, and exhibits at the North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum.

cards.title: Trace geologic time together
cards.subtitle: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.notes: Start with the life-size T. rex and Triceratops casts, then follow the exhibits from ancient geology toward early human history.
cards.short_summary: A gallery walk through North Dakota’s deep past.
cards.evidence_claim: The Adaptation Gallery interprets North Dakota geology and life from 600 million years ago to the appearance of humans, including life-sized T. rex and Triceratops casts; museum admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Exhibits | North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.access_notes: At 612 East Boulevard Avenue. Museum admission is always free; check the museum’s current hours before going.

cards.title: Follow the Early Peoples timeline
cards.subtitle: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.notes: Move through artifacts and the Double Ditch Indian Village cyclorama, using the gallery’s chronology as an easy shared conversation guide.
cards.short_summary: Artifacts and interpretation spanning more than 13,000 years.
cards.evidence_claim: The Innovation Gallery is devoted to Native peoples of North Dakota and includes more than 1,000 artifacts plus a large-scale cyclorama of Double Ditch Indian Village; museum admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Exhibits | North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.access_notes: At 612 East Boulevard Avenue. Museum admission is always free; check the museum’s current hours before going.

cards.title: Compare old and new North Dakota
cards.subtitle: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.notes: Explore the homestead shack, 1950s soda shop, and tractor cab, then pick one gallery theme to discuss before you leave.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on look at the state from 200 years ago to today.
cards.evidence_claim: The Inspiration Gallery covers North Dakota from 200 years ago to contemporary times and includes a homestead shack, 1950s soda shop, and modern tractor cab; museum admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Exhibits | North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.access_notes: At 612 East Boulevard Avenue. Museum admission is always free; check the museum’s current hours before going.

cards.title: See the current Governors Gallery show
cards.subtitle: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.notes: Use this gallery for a shorter stop: read the exhibit introduction, choose a few objects, and compare what each person notices.
cards.short_summary: A changing gallery for temporary and traveling exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Governors Gallery presents temporary and traveling exhibits; museum admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Exhibits | North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.access_notes: At 612 East Boulevard Avenue. Exhibit contents can change; museum admission is always free.

cards.title: Look closely at state-collection art
cards.subtitle: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.notes: Walk the fine-art display at an unhurried pace and trade observations about one work before continuing through the building.
cards.short_summary: A gallery of fine art from North Dakota’s state collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The James E. Sperry Gallery features fine art from the state collections, including works in There’s a Story There: Art in the State Collections; museum admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Exhibits | North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.access_notes: At 612 East Boulevard Avenue. Exhibit contents can change; museum admission is always free.

cards.title: Meet beneath the Northern Lights Atrium
cards.subtitle: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.notes: Use the atrium as a clear meetup point, then pause to take in its architecture and symbolism before choosing a gallery route.
cards.short_summary: An architectural museum landmark suited to a low-key meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: The North Dakota Heritage Center identifies the Northern Lights Atrium as a museum space combining architecture and symbolism; admission is free every day.
cards.source_title: About the Facility | North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.access_notes: At 612 East Boulevard Avenue. Admission is free every day; follow posted museum rules.

cards.title: Walk the Pembina River Plaza
cards.subtitle: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum grounds
cards.notes: Step outside to inspect the geological specimens, then loop back into the museum without needing to make this a long outdoor commitment.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor plaza with specimens from the state’s geologic past.
cards.evidence_claim: The outdoor Pembina River Plaza features specimens from North Dakota’s geologic past, and the Heritage Center states that admission is free every day.
cards.source_title: About the Facility | North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.access_notes: On the museum grounds at 612 East Boulevard Avenue. Admission is free every day; dress for weather.

cards.title: Follow the Corridor of History tracks
cards.subtitle: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.notes: Walk the corridor in chronological order and look down for changing tracks, from dinosaur prints to moccasins and railroad rails.
cards.short_summary: A connective museum route with visual time cues in the floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Tracks and footprints in the Corridor of History change as visitors move chronologically through the museum galleries; museum admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Floor Prints and Tracks | North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.access_notes: Inside the museum at 612 East Boulevard Avenue. Admission is always free; follow the chronological route at your own pace.

cards.title: Find Dakota the Dinomummy
cards.subtitle: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.notes: Make the preserved hadrosaur your scavenger-hunt stop, then use the nearby gallery exhibits to connect its fossil story to the landscape.
cards.short_summary: A named dinosaur specimen with rare preserved skin.
cards.evidence_claim: Dakota is a mummified hadrosaur with rare skin preservation and is described by the museum as scientifically important; museum admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Skylight Icons | North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.access_notes: Inside the museum at 612 East Boulevard Avenue. Admission is always free; ask staff for wayfinding if needed.

cards.entity_name: Adaptation Gallery: Geologic Time Learning Lab
cards.title: Try the geology learning lab
cards.subtitle: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.notes: Watch for the fluorescent-mineral display and use the lab prompts to compare rocks, fossils, and the processes that formed them.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on space connected to the geologic-time gallery.
cards.evidence_claim: The Adaptation Gallery Learning Lab offers fluorescent minerals, a fossil-excavation video, and free demonstrations and hands-on experiences for visitors; museum admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Learning Labs | North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
cards.access_notes: Inside the museum at 612 East Boulevard Avenue. Demonstrations may vary; museum admission is always free.
